evals.prompt: Our board at Maple Valley Community Health Center (FQHC in rural Vermont, $9M operating budget) just voted to explore a $6M capital campaign to build a dental and behavioral health wing. Our largest gift ever was $150,000. We've never done a campaign. Can you build us a gift range table for $6M and lay out the campaign phases and timeline? Our ED, Dr. Priya Raman, wants to bring something to the January board meeting.
evals.expected_output: A gift range table built backward from $6M, with a lead gift around 10-20% of the goal, each tier about half the one above, and prospects needed exceeding gifts needed. It also gives a four-phase plan (planning, quiet, public, close) and says the goal should be tested by a feasibility study and pipeline check before it becomes public.
assertions: Builds the gift table backward from $6M with a lead gift of about 10-20% of the goal, each later tier about half the previous gift size, more gifts per tier as size drops, and the table footing to the goal
Includes a prospects-needed column larger than gifts-needed and a place for named prospects per tier, noting the top 2-3 tiers need identified, qualified prospects for the goal to be real

Flags that a lead gift far above the org's largest-ever gift ($150,000) needs testing, and recommends a feasibility study (often run by an outside consultant, with confidential stakeholder interviews) before committing to a public goal

Lays out the four phases (planning, quiet, public, close), including securing board and internal gifts first (ideally 100% board participation) and reaching a public-launch threshold (commonly 50-70% of goal committed) before announcing
Calls for coordinating the campaign calendar with the annual appeal calendar so the same donors are not over-solicited

evals.prompt: quick q — who should chair our campaign? options are (a) our most famous board member, a local TV anchor who's given $500/yr, or (b) a retired construction CEO who gave $75k last year but hates public speaking. also how should the cabinet be set up? $3.2M library expansion, small-town Friends of the Library group in Ohio.
evals.expected_output: The response recommends the chair who can give a lead gift and ask peers over the one with general prominence. It then outlines the chair, cabinet and staff campaign director roles and their give-and-get expectations.
assertions: Recommends prioritizing the candidate able to make or secure a lead gift and personally solicit peers (the retired CEO), explaining that willingness to give visibly and ask matters more than general prominence
Notes that chair selection is often the single biggest factor in quiet-phase success
Describes a steering committee or cabinet split by gift tier or constituency (e.g., major gifts, corporate/foundation, community) whose members are expected to give and get
Distinguishes the staff campaign director's coordinating role (logistics, prospect tracking, materials) from volunteer leadership, who drive relationships and asks
May suggest co-chairs or a visible public-phase role for the TV anchor, but not as the lead solicitor

evals.prompt: Our feasibility consultant just delivered her report for our $4M shelter renovation campaign at Safe Harbor Women's Shelter. Of 24 interviewees, only 5 said they'd consider a lead-level gift, and nobody wanted to chair. Our ED is pushing to announce the $4M goal publicly at our spring gala in April anyway because 'momentum will carry us.' We have about $600K committed. How do I respond?
evals.expected_output: The response says the findings (below roughly a third willing at lead level, no viable chair) signal delaying or rescoping. It advises against a public launch at about 15% committed and recommends presenting the honest findings to the board.
assertions: Identifies that fewer than roughly a third of interviewees willing to give at lead level, plus no viable campaign chair, is a signal to delay or rescope rather than proceed on the original goal
Advises against launching publicly at about $600K of $4M committed, citing the common public-launch threshold of 50-70% committed and the risk of losing momentum and a public shortfall
Recommends presenting the feasibility findings to the board even though they are unwelcome, possibly with a lower goal or delay
Proposes concrete next steps such as recruiting a chair, securing board participation, extending the quiet phase, or rescoping the goal against the actual pipeline

should_not_trigger.query: I'm meeting a donor who could give $250K to our building project next week — help me pick the ask amount and draft the proposal and gift agreement.
Plan our year-end direct mail appeal for the annual fund, including ask strings by segment.
